claims.claim: In 2024, Stonehenge's Altar Stone was traced to Scotland.
claims.source_checked: Clarke 2024 full text: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07652-1 (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1
claims.note: As a report of what the 2024 paper did, true: title 'A Scottish provenance for the Altar Stone of Stonehenge', published 14 August 2024; abstract: 'remarkable similarity to the Old Red Sandstone of the Orcadian Basin in northeast Scotland'; body: data 'indicate that the Altar Stone of Stonehenge has a provenance from the ORS in the Orcadian Basin of northeast Scotland'. See claim 3 for what the hook leaves a swiping viewer believing.

claims.claim: Exactly where it came from is still unknown.
claims.source_checked: Pirrie 2026 full text: https://www.lyellcollection.org/doi/full/10.1144/jgs2026-090 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1144/jgs2026-090), abstract, Introduction, Discussion, Conclusions; Clarke 2026 full text: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jqs.70080 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1002/jqs.70080); Parker Pearson 2024 full text PDF: https://journals.uclpress.co.uk/ai/article/3293/galley/18572/download/ (doi:10.14324/AI.27.1.13); Crossref record
claims.note: Literally matches Pirrie 2026 abstract ('the exact provenance of the Altar Stone is as yet unknown') and Clarke 2026 ('source location within this large basin remains unresolved'), and 'still' holds (Parker Pearson 2024: 'As yet, the actual outcrop ... is unknown'). But 'Exactly where', right after 'traced to Scotland', presupposes the region is settled and only the spot is open. Pirrie 2026 does more than say the exact outcrop is unknown. Introduction: Clarke 2024 'used the dating of zircon, apatite and rutile grains ... to infer that it was derived from the Orcadian Basin of NE Scotland. However, as presented below, detailed multi-proxy characterization of the Altar Stone raises questions over this interpretation.' Discussion: 'chrome spinel is very scarce in the Orcadian Basin ORS, which may indicate that an origin from this part of NE Scotland needs re-evaluating'; ORS 'from the Scottish Midland Valley to the Anglo-Welsh borderland' and Lower Paleozoic rocks of the Southern Uplands 'and their equivalent in western Ireland' remain possible on heavy-mineral grounds; the 2024 grain ages 'do[es] not exclude a potential source for the Altar Stone from the Carboniferous' (ORS judged 'more likely' on isotopes). Conclusions: 'the provenance of the Altar Stone has yet to be determined with confidence.' Clarke 2026 disagrees (Caithness 'the closest match', source 'within this large basin remains unresolved'). Per A3 the narrower claim is that the source itself is not settled. Change to wording that does not presuppose Scotland, e.g. 'Now a newer study questions that: where it came from is still unknown.' and record the Clarke 2026 vs Pirrie 2026 disagreement in SOURCES (the current SOURCES quotes only Pirrie's abstract and says Pirrie 'narrows the source down rather than overturning the 2024 result', which its Introduction and Discussion do not support: 'raises questions over this interpretation').

claims.claim: Hook as heard by a viewer who swipes at second two: 'the Altar Stone comes from Scotland (only the exact spot is unknown)'
claims.source_checked: Pirrie 2026 full text: https://www.lyellcollection.org/doi/full/10.1144/jgs2026-090 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1144/jgs2026-090), abstract, Introduction, Discussion, Conclusions; Clarke 2026 full text: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jqs.70080 (via Firecrawl; doi:10.1002/jqs.70080); Clarke 2024 full text: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07652-1 (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1
claims.note: The first sentence alone, and the pair together, leave the viewer believing Scotland is established. The 2024 result is real and Clarke 2026 still favours NE Scotland, but Pirrie 2026 (three of the 2024 authors among its 13) says the multi-proxy data 'raises questions over this interpretation', that an NE Scotland origin 'needs re-evaluating', and that 'the provenance ... has yet to be determined with confidence'. A4: the hook must carry the correction. Fix the second sentence as in claim 2 so that within the hook the viewer hears the Scottish attribution is now disputed; do not overcorrect to 'not from Scotland' (no paper says that).

claims.claim: The ages of tiny mineral grains inside it matched sandstone in the northeast.
claims.source_checked: Clarke 2024 full text: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07652-1 (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1
claims.note: Clarke 2024 dated zircon, apatite and rutile from two Altar Stone fragments; grains 'typically 10-40 µm wide' (tiny); 'Detrital age comparisons ... reveal a remarkable similarity to the Old Red Sandstone of the Orcadian Basin in northeast Scotland'; apatite age components from Caithness and Orkney 'match those from the Altar Stone'; KS test fails to reject same distribution. Past tense reports the 2024 finding. Caveat for context: the zircon ages are equally indistinguishable from Svalbard ORS (Clarke 2024) and Pirrie 2026 says they 'do not exclude' a Carboniferous source; 'matched' is still true as stated.
